t: Which part of the cycle is it?
key: Sort each finding by the hormone that causes it: estradiol drives the follicular phase, the LH surge marks ovulation, and progesterone defines the luteal phase.
items: Estradiol without progesterone makes straight, dividing glands in the first half of the cycle.
Estradiol rising from the dominant follicle
The dominant follicle's granulosa cells aromatize androgens, so estradiol climbs before ovulation.
FSH highest at the start of the phase
Falling luteal hormones release FSH at cycle start to recruit the next cohort.
Length varies from cycle to cycle
Follicle selection takes a variable time, so this phase sets the cycle length.
Two days of high estradiol flip feedback and release the surge that triggers ovulation.
The LH surge restarts meiosis, so meiosis I finishes just before the follicle ruptures.
Peak estradiol just before ovulation makes mucus watery and stretchy so sperm can pass.
Follicle rupture can irritate the peritoneum, causing one-sided pain at ovulation.
Progesterone turns glands coiled and vacuolated after ovulation.
The luteinized follicle secretes progesterone for about 14 days after ovulation.
Progesterone raises the hypothalamic set point, so temperature stays up through this phase.
The corpus luteum's lifespan fixes this phase unless hCG rescues it.
